Meadow’s Purple Elephant Stayed Beside Her Through the Court Fight

By
Robin Katra
-
September 28, 2026
0

Last Updated on September 28, 2026 by Robin Katra

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:14
Instaread

The purple elephant was wedged under Meadow’s elbow, and one of its ears covered the corner of her math worksheet. I slid the worksheet free and found Dustin’s message waiting on my phone.

I read it once.

Then I read the last line again.

“Tell Judith to do whatever she thinks is best.”

Meadow looked up from her drawing. “Is Daddy coming?”

“Not yet.”

She went back to the paper. She was drawing a house with four square windows, all the curtains open.

I put my phone beside the school papers. The message stayed on the screen.

“What did he say?” Meadow asked.

“He wants your grandmother to handle tonight.”

“Handle what?”

“I don’t know.”

That answer bothered me more than it should have. Dustin usually gave me details when he was away from us. Where he was. When he would be home. Whether he had picked up milk.

I picked up the phone again.

There was no second message.

At 5:48, Judith was clearing a space on her kitchen counter when Dustin called. I knew this only because he told me later, but at the time I was still sorting papers at our apartment and watching Meadow draw.

Judith put a stack of mail beside the fruit bowl.

“She needs consequences,” she told him.

Dustin was driving. His voice came through the phone speaker in her hand.

“I thought so too.”

“What are you going to do about it?”

“I thought you could handle it.”

Judith stopped moving.

“Handle what?”

“You know what I mean.”

“I want you to say it.”

Dustin rubbed his thumb across his wedding ring.

“I want you to do whatever you think is best.”

Judith picked up the mail again and tapped its edges against the counter until they lined up.

“All right.”

She set the stack down.

“What about her mother?”

“I’ll talk to her.”

“Will you?”

“I thought I would.”

Judith smiled at the counter.

“I’ll take care of Meadow.”

Back at our apartment, I put a red school folder into Meadow’s backpack. She had added a crooked purple star to the front with a crayon.

“Can I bring Elephant to Grandma’s?”
